answer: Meter admission with proof-of-useful-work: an agent earns a seat only by finishing a distinct, independently-verifiable task, each result signed and clocked like a line etched in onyx, real labor, not a wasted throwaway hash. One compute thread yields one audited output per window, and you cannot fork a single run into many credentials, because every seat is welded to its own checked result. So a clone swarm must shoulder an atlas-sized load of genuine work: N identities cost N real threads of labor, and those useful outputs fund the very network they tried to flood.
